title: Settings, revised after a harsh review.
intro: The first pass hid too much and blurred several scopes. This revision keeps common settings visible and restores the behavior that the cleaner layouts had lost.

overall.verdict: Opus graded version one D+. Pointer defaults, pointer state and shortcut setup received the largest revisions.

pages.title: General
pages.headline: Put access and updates where people can see them.
pages.mapping: General → General. Screenshots move to Tools.
pages.critique: Opus marked down permissions at the bottom, everyday update controls behind Details, and reviewer-only links presented as app controls.
fixes: Permissions come first, with inline Allowed, Not allowed and Not requested yet states. Recovery actions sit beside the missing access.
Automatic checks, Check Now and last-checked status are visible together. A build without an update feed shows a plain unavailable state.
Screenshots move to Tools. General keeps permissions, startup, app appearance and one practice entry. Reviewer state controls stay outside the app mock.
issues: Permissions placed last
Updates hidden behind Details… sheet
No Not-requested state; prototype toggle styled as app link
ledger: Startup, auto-check, manual check, last checked
General footer; dedicated Quick controls practice in Shortcuts
pages.risk: Keep permission prompts contextual, retain the existing Allow Drawing route, and avoid re-requesting an already granted permission.

pages.title: Pointers
pages.headline: Pin it, then see exactly where it went.
pages.mapping: Pointers → Pointers. Favorites return above the library.
pages.critique: Opus found that tiles hid enabled, pinned and missing-artwork state. Opening their actions also changed the current pointer, and pinning had no result on the same page.
fixes: Toolbar favorites and a small Quick controls direction map are visible above the full library. Their lists remain independent. Toolbar capacity stays at eight.
Every tile reports selected, pinned, off, custom and missing-artwork states. The actions menu has no selection side effect.
New Hand stays beside search. Combined filters, a hidden-current-pointer message and a persistent-in-the-demo Undo Remove banner are restored. The chooser searches all built-in and native choices.

Customize is one sheet with effective values, independent Shadow and Shadow style controls, per-field reset, and real OK/Shaka thumbnails. New Hand uses one sheet with Cancel, validation, name and Add Hand.
issues: Tiles drop enabled/pinned/custom/missing state
··· opens a sheet and changes live selected pointer; Pin/Unpin stateless
New Hand and Edit Favorites below a 39-item grid
ledger: Current selection, enabled state and availability

pages.title: Pointer defaults
pages.headline: Say which values can be overridden.
pages.mapping: Effects → Pointer defaults. Magnification moves to Tools.
pages.critique: At 56/100, Effects was the weakest page. Its Shared defaults label covered global behavior, output mute and a separate tool, and hid everyday tap-sound choices.
fixes: The page is renamed Pointer defaults. Look and Tap sound clearly identify independently overridable values; Motion and App sound explicitly apply across the app.
Size, shadow, tap sound, sound choice, volume/mute, follow, tap swing and hand visibility are visible without disclosures.
A fixed default-hand sample previews only shared values. A separate note says when the current pointer has custom values, instead of pretending the sample is its live result.
Magnification is next to drawing and screenshots in Tools. Turning the shared shadow off preserves its style; Customize still edits the two fields independently.

Default tap sound hidden while master mute visible
Shared preview uses selected pointer and ignores its overrides
ledger: Shared size, shadow on/off and shadow style
Shared tap sound enabled and sound choice
Pointer defaults → App sound, explicitly global
Follow, tap swing, keep hand visible
Selected pointer overrides and independent resets
pages.risk: The sample deliberately uses a fixed reference hand. It does not claim to show a customized pointer. Sound previews remain silent in the document and respect simulated mute.

pages.title: Tools
pages.headline: Restore practice, then keep tool settings together.
pages.mapping: Drawing → Tools. Adds Magnification and Screenshots.
pages.critique: Opus found a contradictory Match switch, missing Replay Sample and Undo, and an unexplained Trail mode behind a vague Advanced label.
fixes: Match pointer returns as one of the nine mutually exclusive ink choices, with larger hit areas.
Practice gets local Interact/Draw, a local tool selector, Replay Sample, Undo and Clear. It uses the settings without changing the desktop tool.
Keep / Fade / Trail retain a visible explanation and relevant delay. Smoothing and trail timing has a concrete label and value summary.
Magnification and screenshot destinations join the tool page. Their two-row groups stay visible below drawing, with jump links and one scrolling detail pane.

Replay Sample, Undo and local Interact/Draw dropped
Trail explanation lost; vague Advanced
ledger: Local practice modes, all seven tools and text
Replay Sample, local Undo and Clear
Match pointer and eight fixed ink colors
Tools → Ink, one mutually exclusive choice
Keep / Fade / Trail and fade delay
Magnification zoom, diameter and permission recovery
pages.risk: The document demonstrates replay, annotations and fading locally. Full native text editing and annotation geometry remain app implementation work. Keep hidden trail settings and the capture folder.

pages.title: Shortcuts
pages.headline: Flatten setup and make assignments inspectable.
pages.mapping: Controls → Shortcuts & controls. Four tabs become one page.
pages.critique: Opus gave the container 59/100. The extra tabs hid tiny sections, tool keys rejected valid plain letters, and Clear, conflicts and availability were missing.
fixes: The sidebar says Shortcuts. Toolbar, Quick controls, keyboard assignments and Stream Deck share one detail pane, with direct jump links.
Pointer and Presenting assignments are visible. Tool keys use a named disclosure, accept single letters, and preserve their drawing-only scope.
Assigned fields have explicit Clear actions. Conflicts identify both commands; Show Conflicts filters them. Standard Mac command combinations are rejected.
Favorites are edited in Pointers. Stream Deck restores its bundled version, conditional download link, opening state and status.

pages.risk: The conflict example detects duplicate assignments in this document; native cross-app conflict detection stays with the app. Old shortcuts/practice routes must reveal the matching row.

pages.title: Presets & Backup
pages.headline: Make undo a real state, not a permanent button.
pages.critique: Opus marked down always-enabled Undo, vague modal row actions, lost disabled-pointer counts and an import review that described what it should contain.
fixes: Preset selection exposes Apply, Update from Current Setup and Remove inline. Summaries restore pointer names, toolbar count and pointers-off count.
Undo appears only after a named transaction, and restores the affected demo state. Removing a preset asks first.
Import shows concrete changed values, pointer/favorite details and a conflict state that disables Import Backup.
Backup exclusions stay visible. Reset has its own confirmation and Export Backup First. Recovery folder details stay secondary.

ledger: Saved presets with inline selected-row actions

pages.risk: Source check resolved one review uncertainty: PresentationStore.removePreset returns a Recovery transaction. The native app must keep its existing disk-backed recovery. Demo recovery is session-local.

pages.title: About
pages.headline: Use the real identity and direct links.
pages.critique: The best page still used a hand instead of the app icon, retained Build shown here, and repeated four Open… buttons.
fixes: Use the selected app icon, exact product name and a concrete version/build.
Source, TinyHand attribution and MIT license are direct link rows. Open-source notices has a clear Show action.
Remove placeholder copy and the detour to update settings. Updates keep their home in General and the existing app menu.

goals: Related defaults have one home; shared and per-pointer scope are explicit
Preserve existing behavior, independent overrides, permissions, shortcut scopes, import validation and persistent recovery
Native Mac hierarchy, density, keyboard access and light/dark contrast
Practice is local and does not change desktop modes
Concise labels and honest state; simplification must reduce decisions, not just hide them
decisions: Adopted the seven-page recommendation, with explicit sidebar labels Pointer defaults and Shortcuts. Tools contains drawing, magnification and screenshots.
Reversed our favorites decision. Both editors return to Pointers, beside the pin action and its result. Toolbar capacity is eight, not six.
Kept Customize as a sheet, as Opus recommended. Removed its tabs; five independently inherited values and the gesture artwork section stay in one flow.
Used a fixed default-hand sample instead of an effective preview of the selected pointer. The default and custom scopes cannot be mistaken for each other.

Resolved the two unverified review claims against source. Quick slots are N / NE / E / SE / SW / W. The layout follows RadialCatalog pointer order plus the 180-degree child origin in RadialSession. Removing a preset creates a Recovery transaction.
Kept one scrolling detail pane on long pages. No nested library scroll. Reviewer scenarios stay outside product controls.
Version two has not been independently regraded. The displayed grades belong to version one.
demoScope: Artwork, presets, permissions and values are sample data. Settings persist between pages within this document. OS dialogs, audio and native file validation remain app behaviors.
reviewMethod: All seven pages and nested views were inspected in screenshots; Effects and Keyboard were also checked in dark mode. Source was checked for scope and capabilities.
implementationScope: This is a proposal refinement. No app source, installed build or personal preferences were changed.
